[[File:Formula_One_constructors%27_championship_trophy_2012-2013_Red_Bull_Racing.jpg|thumb|right|upright|alt=A silver trophy with team logos on it in a glass case|The constructors' trophy, as presented to [[Red Bull Racing|Red Bull]]-[[Renault in Formula One|Renault]] at the completion of the {{F1|2012}} season]]

{{Formula One|lists}} 
[[Formula One]] (F1) is the highest class of [[Open wheel car|open-wheeled]] [[motorsport]] defined by the [[Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile]] (FIA), motorsport's world governing body.<ref>{{cite web|title=About FIA|date=24 February 2015 |url=https://www.fia.com/organisation|access-date=13 April 2020|publisher=Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA)|archive-date=1 May 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200501222208/https://www.fia.com/organisation|url-status=live}}</ref> The "formula" in the name refers to a set of rules to which all participants and cars must conform.<ref>{{cite web|last=Williamson|first=Martin|title=A brief history of Formula One|url=http://en.espn.co.uk/f1/motorsport/story/3831.html|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=23 December 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150406023200/http://en.espn.co.uk/f1/motorsport/story/3831.html|archive-date=6 April 2015}}</ref> The [[List of Formula One seasons|F1 World Championship season]] consists of a series of races, known as {{not a typo|[[List of Formula One Grands Prix|Grands Prix]]}}, held usually on purpose-built [[List of Formula One circuits|circuits]], and in a few cases on [[Street circuit|closed city streets]].<ref>{{cite book|last1=Hughes|first1=Mark|title=The Concise Encyclopedia of Formula 1|last2=Tremayne|first2=David|author-link1=Mark Hughes (motorsport)|author-link2=David Tremayne|url=https://archive.org/details/conciseencyclope0000trem_m9u1|publisher=Parragon|year=2002|isbn=0-75258-766-8|pages=82–83|url-access=registration}}</ref> The World Constructors' Championship is presented by the FIA to the most successful F1 [[List of Formula One constructors|constructor]] over the course of the season through a [[List of Formula One points systems|points system]] based on individual Grand Prix results. Constructors' Championship points are calculated by adding points scored in each race by any driver for that constructor.<ref>{{cite web|date=7 April 2020|title=2020 Formula One Sporting Regulations|url=https://www.fia.com/sites/default/files/2020_formula_1_sporting_regulations_-_iss_6_-_2020-04-07.pdf|access-date=15 April 2020|publisher=Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA)|pages=3–4|archive-date=12 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200412175805/https://www.fia.com/sites/default/files/2020_formula_1_sporting_regulations_-_iss_6_-_2020-04-07.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref> According to FIA regulations, the constructor of a chassis and an engine of a [[Formula One car]] is a person or corporate entity that owns the intellectual rights to the chassis and the engine of the car that a team/entrant enters into a competition.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Verlin|first=Kurt|date=10 October 2017|title=Quick Guide to Formula One Constructors|url=https://thenewswheel.com/quick-guide-to-formula-one-constructors/|access-date=2 December 2020|website=The News Wheel|language=en-US|archive-date=31 December 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201231220547/https://thenewswheel.com/quick-guide-to-formula-one-constructors/|url-status=live}}</ref>

From the inaugural season of the World Constructors' Championship in {{F1|1958}} up until the {{F1|1978}} season only the highest-scoring driver in each race for each constructor contributed points towards the World Constructors' Championship (then officially as the ''International Cup for Formula One Constructors''); since the {{F1|1979}} season points from all cars entered by each constructor have counted towards their championship total.<ref>{{cite book|last=Hayhoe|first=David|title=Kimberley Grand Prix Data Book: Formula 1 Racing Facts and Figures 1950 to Date|url=https://archive.org/details/kimberleygrandpr0000hayh|publisher=Haynes Publishing|location=Sparkford, England|year=1989|pages=8|isbn=0-946132-63-1|url-access=registration}}</ref> The Constructors' Championship is won when it is no longer mathematically possible for another constructor to overtake another's points total regardless of the outcome of the remaining races,<ref>{{Cite web|last=Galloway|first=James|date=29 October 2020|title=Mercedes: How they can clinch F1 Constructors' Championship at Emilia Romagna GP|url=https://www.skysports.com/f1/news/12472/12115876/mercedes-how-they-can-clinch-f1-constructors-championship-at-emilia-romagna-gp|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201101035215/https://www.skysports.com/f1/news/12472/12115876/mercedes-how-they-can-clinch-f1-constructors-championship-at-emilia-romagna-gp|archive-date=1 November 2020|access-date=18 November 2020|publisher=[[Sky Sports]]}}</ref> although it is not officially awarded until the [[FIA Prize Giving Ceremony]] held in various cities following the conclusion of the season.<ref>{{cite web|last=Murphy|first=Luke|date=8 December 2018|title=Hamilton & Mercedes F1 officially crowned at FIA Prize Giving Ceremony|url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/hamilton-mercedes-f1-officially-crowned-at-fia-prize-giving-ceremony-66698/3222469/|access-date=19 September 2020|work=[[Motorsport.com]]|archive-date=8 December 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201208073421/https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/hamilton-mercedes-f1-officially-crowned-at-fia-prize-giving-ceremony-66698/3222469/|url-status=live}}</ref>

The Constructors' Championship was first awarded, as the ''International Cup for Formula One Manufacturers'', in {{F1|1958}} to [[Vanwall]].<ref>{{Cite news|last=Hughes|first=Peter|date=1 August 2018|title=Vanwall's constructors' championship in '58 changed Grand Prix racing forever|work=[[Autoweek]]|url=https://www.autoweek.com/car-life/a1703106/vanwalls-constructors-championship-58-changed-grand-prix-racing-forever/|url-status=live|access-date=18 November 2020|archive-date=21 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200421044140/https://www.autoweek.com/car-life/a1703106/vanwalls-constructors-championship-58-changed-grand-prix-racing-forever/}}</ref> In {{F1|1981}} this name was officially changed to the ''World Constructors' Championship''. The makes of both chassis and an engine are included in the constructor name.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Diepraam|first=Mattijs|date=3 January 2008|title=Poachers turned gamekeepers: how the FOCA became the new FIA: Part 4: 1981 – long live the FIA F1 World Championship|url=http://8w.forix.com/fiasco-81.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080131164252/http://8w.forix.com/fiasco-81.html|archive-date=31 January 2008|access-date=10 March 2024|website=8W|publisher=Forix}}</ref>

Out of the 170 chassis constructors that have entered an F1 Grand Prix,<ref>{{Cite web|title=F1 Stats Zone – Results by Team|url=https://www.skysports.com/f1/stats/teams/search|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190601035051/https://www.skysports.com/f1/stats/teams/search|archive-date=1 June 2019|access-date=18 November 2020|publisher=Sky Sports}}</ref> a total of 15 have won the Championship in its 68 seasons. [[Scuderia Ferrari|Ferrari]] holds the record for the highest number of World Constructors' Championships victories, having won the title on 16 occasions. [[McLaren]] are in second position with ten Constructors' Championships. [[Williams Racing|Williams]] are in third position with nine Constructors' Championships and [[Mercedes-Benz in Formula One|Mercedes]] are in fourth with eight titles.<ref name="CF1Constructors">{{Cite web|title=Constructors' Championships|url=https://www.chicanef1.com/allconsts.pl|access-date=20 June 2026|publisher=ChicaneF1}}</ref><ref name="8WChamps">{{cite web|last=Diepraam|first=Mattijs|date=November 3, 2019|title=European & World Champions|url=http://8w.forix.com/6thgear/worldchampions.html|access-date=7 December 2025|publisher=8W}}</ref> With 16 titles, Ferrari has amassed the highest number of Constructors' Championships as an engine manufacturer, followed by [[Renault in Formula One|Renault]], Mercedes, [[Ford Motor Company|Ford]] and [[Honda in Formula One|Honda]] with twelve, twelve, ten and six titles, respectively.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Statistics Engines - World Champion titles - Chronology • STATS F1|url=https://www.statsf1.com/en/statistiques/moteur/champion/chronologie.aspx|access-date=20 June 2026|website=www.statsf1.com}}</ref> Mercedes holds the record for the most consecutive constructors' titles with eight between the {{F1|2014}} and the {{F1|2021}} seasons.<ref name=ConsecutiveWins>{{Cite web|title=Statistics Constructors – World Champion titles consecutively|url=https://www.statsf1.com/en/statistiques/constructeur/champion/consecutif.aspx|access-date=20 June 2026|publisher=StatsF1}}</ref> 

All but 17 titles (16 titles won by Italian-built Ferrari chassis and 1 title won by French-built [[Equipe Matra Sports|Matra]] chassis) have been won by chassis that were designed and constructed in the United Kingdom.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Barretto|first=Lawrence|date=26 June 2013|title=Motorsport Valley – the home of Formula 1|language=en-GB|publisher=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/formula1/23048643|url-status=live|access-date=2020-08-20|archive-date=27 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200927174311/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/formula1/23048643}}</ref> On twelve occasions, the World Constructors' Champion team has not contained the World Drivers' Champion for that season.<ref name="8WChamps" /> All titles but one  (in {{F1|1969}} Matra cars were entered by [[Ken Tyrrell]]'s [[Privateer (motorsport)|privateer]] team [[Tyrrell Racing|Matra International]]) have been won by cars that were entered by [[Factory-backed|works teams]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Diepraam|first=Mattijs|title=Ken's team at the height of its powers|url=http://8w.forix.com/tyrrell73.html|publisher=8W|date=November 2000|access-date=18 November 2020|archive-date=17 July 2006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060717234152/http://8w.forix.com/tyrrell73.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Matra Sports SARL|url=https://www.grandprix.com/gpe/con-matra.html|publisher=GrandPrix.com|access-date=18 November 2020|archive-date=1 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201101071014/https://www.grandprix.com/gpe/con-matra.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Among drivers that have contributed with at least a single point to the constructors' title, [[Lewis Hamilton]] has contributed to the most with eight constructors' titles, all of them with Mercedes.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Southwell|first=Hazel|date=12 December 2021|title=Mercedes seal record eighth consecutive constructors title as Hamilton misses driver's crown|url=https://www.racefans.net/2021/12/12/mercedes-seal-record-eighth-consecutive-constructors-title-as-hamilton-misses-drivers-crown/|access-date=12 December 2021|publisher=RaceFans|archive-date=12 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211212155101/https://www.racefans.net/2021/12/12/mercedes-seal-record-eighth-consecutive-constructors-title-as-hamilton-misses-drivers-crown/|url-status=live}}</ref>

==By chassis constructor==
[[Image:Luca_Badoer_2008_test.jpg|thumb|right|220px|[[Scuderia Ferrari|Ferrari]] holds the record of most World Constructors' Championship titles having won 16 times. Their first was in {{F1|1961}}, and their most recent title was won in {{F1|2008}}. ([[Ferrari F2008]] pictured)]]
[[Image:Rosberg_Hamilton_-_2016_Monaco_GP_2.jpg|thumb|right|220px|[[Mercedes-Benz in Formula One|Mercedes]] won a record-making eight consecutive World Constructors' Championship titles spanning from {{F1|2014}} to {{F1|2021}}. ([[Mercedes F1 W07 Hybrid]] pictured)]]
[[Image:FIA_F1_Austria_2023_Nr._1_(1)_(cropped).jpg|thumb|right|220px|The [[Red Bull Racing RB19]] is the most dominant car to win a World Constructors' Championship, winning 21 of 22 Grands Prix across the {{F1|2023}} season.]]
[[Image:Las Vegas Grand Prix (54941206297) (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|220px|[[McLaren]], second in all time championships, are the reigning World Constructors' Champions, having won back-to-back titles in {{F1|2024}} and {{F1|2025}}. ([[McLaren MCL39]] pictured)]]

==Consecutive titles==
===By chassis constructor===
There have been nine constructors who have achieved consecutive wins in the World Constructors' Championship. Of those, only Ferrari and Williams have won four sets of consecutive Formula One World Constructors' Championships.<ref name="8WChamps" /><ref name="ConsecutiveWins" />
